short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.say: My socket peaks at 325 V… but it says 230 V?
short_scenes.narration: Volt measures his socket on a scope. The peak is three hundred and twenty five volts, but it's called two hundred and thirty volts. Why?
Square the wave, average it, take the root. That's RMS, the value that heats things like DC would.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: AC keeps changing, so we ask: what DC voltage would heat a heater the same amount? That value is RMS, about seventy one percent of the peak.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.narration: Three twenty five divided by root two is two hundred and thirty.

short_scenes.name: Volt
short_scenes.say: Watch the full video: AC fundamentals!
short_scenes.narration: For the detailed explanation, watch the full video on our channel. It's part of our complete Network Theory course.
